note: Fictional brand. Tick each rule you think the draft breaks, and tick nothing if it breaks none.

rules.title: Calm, expert, warm
rules.text: Write like a dermatologist friend: calm, specific and warm. Explain, don't shout.
rules.yes: Daily Shield sits light on skin, so it is easy to wear every morning.

rules.title: Never hype
rules.text: Velvra never hypes. No slang superlatives, no shouting, no runs of exclamation marks.
rules.yes: Meet Daily Shield SPF 50, made for everyday protection.

rules.title: No fear-based beauty language
rules.text: Never make people feel bad about their skin. Talk about care, not flaws.
rules.yes: Care for skin that sees the sun every day.

rules.title: Tie launches to the pillars
rules.text: Launch messages should connect to our pillars where it makes sense.
rules.yes: Daily protection that helps skin look visibly more even.

rules.title: No instant-results promises
rules.text: Skin changes take weeks. Never promise instant, overnight or vanishing results.
rules.yes: With daily use, skin can look more even over a few weeks.

rules.title: No “chemical-free”
rules.text: Everything is a chemical. Name what the product is free from instead.

rules.title: Daily Shield is a sunscreen
rules.text: Daily Shield is a sunscreen. Never call it a serum or a moisturiser.

rules.title: Use the product name
rules.text: Use “Daily Shield SPF 50”, not “sunblock” or “sun cream”.

rules.title: Claims must match the Claim Ledger
rules.text: Any study or numeric claim must match an approved Claim Ledger fact and use its approved wording. “Clinically proven” is allowed only for clinical facts.

rules.title: No guarantees
rules.text: Never guarantee results or promise anything permanent.

rules.title: Superlatives need a fact
rules.text: Superlatives and comparisons (“best”, “No. 1”, “better than”) need an approved Claim Ledger fact.

rules.title: No medical claims
rules.text: Velvra is cosmetic. Never say a product cures, treats or heals a condition.

rules.title: Study claims need a footnote
rules.text: Every study claim carries a footnote with the study type, size and year.

rules.title: SPF reapply disclaimer
rules.text: Email and website copy that mentions SPF must include the reapply disclaimer.

rules.title: Descriptive link text
rules.text: Link text says where it goes. Never “click here” or “read more”.

rules.title: Readable for the channel
rules.text: Copy meets the readability target for its channel (Flesch reading ease).

rules.title: Hashtags, emoji and capitals
rules.text: Use CamelCase hashtags so screen readers read them as words. Keep emoji and ALL-CAPS words within the channel limit.
